title: Florida Atlantic University Receives NIST Grant to Build South Florida Quantum Cybersecurity Workforce Ecosystem - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Florida Atlantic University, working with D-Wave Quantum (QBTS), won a $200,000 NIST RAMPS cooperative agreement to build a South Florida quantum-cybersecurity workforce consortium tied to power-grid protection and FAU’s upcoming on-premises D-Wave Advantage2 system.

insights.claim: FAU, in collaboration with D-Wave Quantum Inc., received a $200,000 NIST RAMPS cooperative agreement to establish a regional quantum cybersecurity workforce consortium across the Palm Beach and Treasure Coast region of South Florida.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small federal grant but a signal that quantum-workforce funding is flowing through cybersecurity channels.

insights.claim: FAU’s award is one of 9 organizations selected across 8 states under the RAMPS program, so the grant is competitive but modest in size.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Scale check: federal quantum workforce dollars here are in the hundreds of thousands, not millions.

insights.claim: The consortium links FAU, D-Wave, InfraGard South Florida, Palm Beach and Broward County public schools, FBI private-sector partners, public utilities and regional employers, spanning K-12 through employment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Ecosystem-building rather than technology; relevant mainly as demand signal for D-Wave’s education/regional strategy.

insights.claim: The curriculum will use FAU’s upcoming on-premises dedicated D-Wave Advantage2 annealing system (4,400+ qubits) on the Boca Raton campus alongside FPL InETech hardware-in-the-loop power simulators.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: D-Wave continues to place on-premises annealers at universities, which supports its system-sales narrative.

insights.claim: The program frames quantum workforce training around securing critical energy infrastructure (power grid, smart spaces, defense networks) against emerging post-quantum cryptographic threats.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Utilities are positioned as an early PQC-workforce demand center.
